Shortly after the Ratatosk Express failed to emerge from the Bifrost, a small group of bandits arrived to prey on the chaos. Their clothing and weapons were utterly alien, and it took almost 20 years to capture them. Even stranger, in the 60 years of their imprisonment, they have stubbornly refused to age. They have, however, shown an affinity for technology beyond what we know. If anyone still living understands the Bifrost, it'll be them. The first that matters, that really matters is from the locomotive. Thor and Sigyn standing in the engine room, staring towards where the engine should be. But there is no engine. Instead, a man lies upon a silver altar. His name is Kvasir, a low level member of the Midgardian resistance, but that doesn't matter. What matters is the dozen tubes and feed lines plugged into his veins, pumping blood through the arcane glyphs and blood channels and gears and sigils that line the chamber. The metal is the same as that which makes the track, and it hums like a far off chant.​ Judging by their faces, neither Thor nor Sigyn had any idea what was in this room. After a few moments of paralysis, Sigyn runs to Kvasir, pulling tubes out of him, blood seeping - oozing from his wounds. Thor begins pulling levers and throwing switches seemingly at random, causing the glyphs and channels to move and warp their constellations. Then they stop. It isn't clear whether it was removing Kvasir or Thor meddling with the controls, but both of them can sense that something has changed. Something has gone very, very wrong.​

"I have a beautiful vision to share with you...that has inspired me very much and has become a new song." "This vision was shared with me as I was helping someone else with their healing. It involves many cultures, it is global in its true message, it is not one I have personally experienced, although I have experienced one that is very similar." "The Chinese woman and her American daughter stood silently in a grotto of all these powerful and beautiful trees. The Chinese mother said with such great assurance and boldness: 'Who are all these people? So many people! And horses everywhere. Beautiful horses, so many of them!’" Beautiful horses Beautiful horses, so many of them "'And so many beautiful horses, everything is so beautiful and peaceful and serene! It's absolutely beautiful.’ And she kept repeating this over and over and over..." "And she kept repeating this over and over and over..." "And she kept repeating this over and over and over..." "I asked, 'Did your mother say they were...peaceful? And in a serene state? Not war-torn or troubled? But serene and in harmony?' 'Total harmony! Very peaceful,' was how the Chinese woman described them. And then she added that she also saw a beautiful waterfall filled with life-giving water, and it was flowing under the people who were at the water's feet, and looking up, she saw a magnificent chief." "'Who are all these people? So many people! And horses everywhere. Beautiful horses, so many of them!'" Beautiful horses Beautiful horses, so many of them "Because our world today has so many imbalances that are rapidly escalating, involving environmental issues and conflicts and cultures. It struck me: here was a people who tried to explain this harmony between man and the land. And no one would listen. Another word seemed even more urgently needed by our world as we faced so many earthquakes and tsunamis and global warming escalates, and other disasters are multiplying. I began to wonder: if these people might still be nearby, perhaps in another dimension, close, but yet apart."
